Bi Gun’s biography spells the place “Yuanqu,” and the same spelling appears in the Han shu geography (Hanshi shang in these notes), fascicle three of the Continued Han treatise, the Song shu gazetteer (Song zhi 1), the Wei shu terrain chapter (Hou Wei zhi 2), and the Sui shu geography (Sui zhi zhong).
248
湖陸原作「陸湖」。 舉正：當作「湖陸」，見《左傳》襄公十九年杜注。 斠注：水經濟水、泗水注亦作「湖陸」。 按：漢志上、《續漢志·三》謂本曰湖陵，莽改湖陸。 今據乙正。
The line originally reversed the order to “Luhu” instead of Hulu. It must be Hulu, as Du Yu’s gloss on the nineteenth year of Duke Xiang in the Zuo zhuan shows. Supporting note: the Shui jing’s passages on the Ji and Si rivers likewise record Hulu. The upper Han treatise and fascicle three of the Continued Han explain that the place was first called Huling until Wang Mang’s reform renamed it Hulu. The characters are transposed accordingly.
249
烏下聚馬與龍晉書地理志注後簡稱馬校：「烏」當作「嶲」。 《續漢志·三》作「嶲下聚」，劉昭注引《左傳》僖公二十六年杜注作「嶲下」。
At Wuxia, Ma Yulong’s commentary on the Jin shu geography—cited below as Ma’s Collation—shows the character for “crow” should be read as Xi, the river name. Fascicle three of the Continued Han has Xixia hamlet, and Liu Zhao, citing Du Yu on the twenty-sixth year of Duke Xi, records the same Xixia form.
250
南城原作「南武城」。 考異：景獻羊皇后、惠羊皇后、羊祜傳、宋書羊欣、羊元保傳並云泰山南城人，宋、齊、隋志皆稱南城，惟晉志多一「武」字，殆因下文有「南武陽」而衍一「武」字。 按：錢說是，今據刪。
The manuscript first read “Nanwucheng” where only Nancheng is meant. Note: Empresses Jingxian and Hui of the Yang clan, the biography of Yang Hu, and the Song shu lives of Yang Xin and Yang Yuanbao all list them as natives of Nancheng in Taishan; Song, Qi, and Sui gazetteers likewise write Nancheng, whereas the Jin treatise alone inserts an extra “martial,” perhaps because “Nanwuyang” appears just below and the eye slipped. Qian’s judgment holds, and the intrusive graph is struck.
251
牟原作「東牟」。 考異：「東」字衍。 漢志上、《續漢志·三》泰山郡有牟縣，即春秋牟國，與東萊之東牟非一地。 羊祜傳詔以泰山之南武陽、牟、南城、梁父、平陽爲南城郡，是晉時已名牟縣也。 按：宋志一、《左傳》桓公十五年注「泰山牟縣」，均亦無「東」字，今據刪。
The line first read “Dongmou” although the county is simply Mou. The character “east” is a spurious accretion. The upper Han treatise and fascicle three of the Continued list Mou county in Taishan, the old polity of Mou, which has nothing to do with Dongmou in Donglai. Yang Hu’s biography records an edict that grouped Nanwuyang, Mou, Nancheng, Liangfu, and Pingyang in Taishan into Nancheng commandery, so by Jin times the place was already plain “Mou county.” Song zhi 1 and Du Yu’s gloss on the fifteenth year of Duke Huan both speak of “Mou county in Taishan” without an extra “east,” so the stray character is removed.
252
長平馬校：縣已見前潁川郡，此誤複出。
Changping: Ma’s Collation notes the county was already tallied under Yingchuan; this second listing is a mistaken repeat.
253
竺邑《方校》：武陔傳，「沛國竹邑人」，此作「竺邑」，似誤。 斠注：魏志明紀、胡質傳引虞預晉書、宋書州郡志、水經睢水注引李奇說皆作「竹邑」。 竺邑即竹邑，本漢縣，有竹邑侯張壽碑。 按：《漢志·上》、《續漢志·二》、《後漢書·明八王傳》、《吳志·薛綜傳》、《隋志·下》彭城郡符離下注並作「竹」。
Zhuyi: Fang’s Collation points out that Wu Gai’s biography calls him a native of Zhuyi in Pei with the “bamboo” radical, whereas here a near-homophone appears and is probably wrong. Cross-checks in the Wei Chronicle’s basic annals, the biography of Hu Zhi citing Yu Yu’s Jin shu, the Song gazetteer, and Li Qi’s gloss in the Shui jing commentary on the Sui consistently spell the place with the bamboo graph. The intended name is Zhuyi, a Han county; a memorial stele for Marquis Zhang Shou of Zhuyi still attests it. The upper Han treatise, fascicle two of the Continued Han, the lives of the Later Han’s eight Ming princes, Xue Zong’s biography in the Wu zhi, and the gloss on Fuli under Pengcheng in the lower Sui gazetteer all keep the bamboo radical.
254
蕃各本作「番」，今從宋本作「蕃」，與漢志下、《續漢志·二》合。
Witnesses print a homophone of the place name, but the Song edition’s full form matches the lower Han treatise and fascicle two of the Continued Han.
255
縣八十三「三」，各本作「二」，今從殿本作「三」，與實領縣數合。
The tally “eighty-three counties” appears as “eighty-two” in most copies; the palace manuscript’s “three” matches the real number of counties governed.
256
易城漢志上、《續漢志·二》、後魏志上及後漢書劉虞傳並無「城」字。
For Yicheng, the upper Han treatise, fascicle two of the Continued Han, the upper Wei geography, and Liu Yu’s Later Han biography omit the extra graph “walled town.”
257
戶一萬八千一百「八千」，各本作「六千」，今從殿本作「八千」，與統計戶數相符。
The census line “eighteen thousand one hundred households” is corrupted to “sixteen thousand” in many witnesses; the palace manuscript’s “eight” tallies with the aggregate figures.
258
陰氣雍閼也「陰」下原有「陽」字。 斠注：類聚六、御覽一六四引太康地記均無「陽」字。 按：無「陽」字是，今據刪。
In the sentence about yin vapor dammed and stalled, an intrusive “yang” once stood after “yin.” Parallel citations in Yiwen leiju, book 6, and Taiping yulan, scroll 164, quoting the Taikang geography, never show the extra “yang.” The shorter reading is sound, and the spurious graph is excised.
259
始平郡泰始二年置「二」，各本作「三」，今從宋本作「二」，與宋志三合。
The founding of Shiping commandery in the second year of Taishi is misdated as the third year in most texts; Song zhi 3 supports the second year, as does the Song exemplar.
260
徙都疑此二字因涉下文「徙都長安」而誤衍。
The phrase “moved the capital” is probably a dittography prompted by “moved the capital to Chang’an” a few lines later.
261
李閏姚萇載記、魏書安定王燮傳皆作「李潤」。
Where the Jin treatise writes Li with the “intercalary” graph, parallel sources such as Yao Chang’s annals and the Wei shu biography of Prince Anding Xie spell the place Li Run with the standard “moisten” character.
262
避文帝諱改也「文」，原誤作「景」，今改正。
The gloss should name Emperor Wen’s taboo, not “Jing”; the mistaken graph is corrected.
263
冥安「冥」原作「宜」。 《畢校》：應作「冥安」，《元和郡縣志》以縣界冥水爲名。 按：畢說是，今據改。 下同。
For Ming’an the first character was wrongly copied as “suitable” instead of “dark.” Bi’s Collation argues for “Ming’an,” the form preserved in the Yuanhe junxian zhi, which explains the name from the Ming River along the border. Bi’s judgment stands, and the text is emended. The same correction applies to the entries that follow.
264
深泉考異：「淵泉」作「深泉」，避唐諱。
Shenquan replaces Yuanquan to skirt the Tang taboo on “abyss.”
265
張駿分武威武興西平張掖酒泉建康西海西郡湟河晉興廣武合十一郡爲涼州原缺「西海」，「廣武」誤作「須武」，今據《後魏書·張駿傳》補改。
Where Zhang Jun grouped Wuwei, Wuxing, Xiping, Zhangye, Jiuquan, Jiankang, Xihai, Xijun, Huanghe, Jinxing, and Guangwueleven commanderies in allinto Liangzhou, the manuscript dropped Xihai and garbled “Guangwu” as “Xuwu”; both errors are repaired from the Later Wei history’s biography of Zhang Jun.
266
敦煌晉昌高昌西域都護戊己校尉玉門大護軍三郡三營爲沙州原缺「高昌」，「戊己」誤作「張茂以」，今據《後魏書·張駿傳》增改。
The roster that makes Dunhuang, Jinchang, Gaochang, the Western Regions protector, the Wuji colonel, and the Yumen grand guardthree commanderies alongside three garrisonsinto Sha province originally omitted Gaochang and mangled “Wuji” into a phrase about Zhang Mao; the Later Wei biography of Zhang Jun supplies the fixes.
267
晉復爲天水「晉」當作「魏」。 魏時有天水郡，見三國志姜維傳及注、楊阜傳、曹真傳、張既傳、閻溫傳。
The word “Jin” should read “Wei”: Wei times again saw a Tianshui commandery. Wei already maintained a Tianshui commandery, documented in the lives of Jiang Wei (and Pei’s notes), Yang Fu, Cao Zhen, Zhang Ji, and Yan Wen.
268
及獻帝初平六年趙一清水經注釋三三：全祖望謂初平只四年，無六年，當作元年。
On Emperor Xian’s sixth year of Chuping, Zhao Yi’s commentary to the Shui jing zhu cites Quan Zuwang’s remark that Chuping lasted but four years and should begin with the first year of that era, not a nonexistent sixth.
269
縣四十四各本作「縣三十三」，今從殿本作「縣四十四」，與統計實數合。
Where copies say “thirty-three counties,” the palace manuscript’s “forty-four” matches the actual tally in the tables.
270
蜀置《畢校》：譙周《巴記》，建安六年劉璋分巴郡墊江以上爲巴西郡。 據此，則巴西郡劉璋時分置。
Annotation on Shu’s foundation: Bi’s Collation cites Qiao Zhou’s Ba Record that in the sixth year of Jian’an Liu Zhang split off the region above Dianjiang in Ba commandery as Baxi commandery. If that entry is sound, Baxi commandery was already peeled off while Liu Zhang still held Ba.
271
魚復各本作「魚腹」，今從宋本作「魚復」。 漢志上、《續漢志·五》、華陽國志一、後漢書張堪傳、蜀志先主傳並作「魚復」。
Most witnesses corrupt the name to the homophone meaning “fish belly,” yet the Song block preserves the ancient “fish-return” spelling. The upper Han treatise, fascicle five of the Continued Han, book one of the Huayang guo zhi, Zhang Kan’s Later Han biography, and the Shu zhi life of the First Lord all agree on Yufu.
272
初平元年劉璋分巴郡立永寧郡考異：劉焉以興平元年卒，子璋始爲益州牧，則初平元年璋尚未牧益州，「初平」當爲「興平」之訛。
The line dating Yongning commandery to the first year of Chuping, when Liu Zhang supposedly split Ba, is dubious: Liu Yan died at the outset of Xingping, and only his son Zhang then took stewardship of Yizhou; in the first year of Chuping Zhang had no mandate there, so “Chuping” is plainly a corruption of Xingping.
273
談指原作「指談」。 斠注：兩漢志、華陽國志四並作「談指」。 按：漢書昭帝紀、前漢紀十六亦作「談指」。 今據乙正。
The two graphs of Tanzhi were reversed to the meaningless sequence “Zitan.” Both Han dynastic gazetteers and book four of the Huayang guo zhi spell the county Tanzhi. The Zhao annals in the Han shu and scroll sixteen of the Qian Han ji record the same form. The characters are transposed back into order.
274
毋歛原作「毋劍」。 斠注：兩漢志、宋志、華陽國志四、水經溫水注皆作「毋歛」。 按：「劍」乃誤字，今改。
The county appears as “Wujian,” importing the graph for “sword” by mistake. The two Han treatises, the Song gazetteer, the Huayang guo zhi, and the Wen River passage of the Shui jing unanimously read Wulian. The intrusive graph is wrong and is replaced.
275
毋掇漢志上「掇」作「棳」，師古曰其字從木。 水經溫水注亦作「毋棳」。
For Wuzhuo the upper Han treatise writes the second syllable with the tree radical, and Yan Shigu remarks that the character belongs to the wood classifier. The Wen River commentary in the Shui jing preserves the same wooden-graph spelling.
276
鐔封「鐔」，各本作「鐸」。 宋本及音義作「鐔」，今從宋本。 與漢志上、《續漢志·五》、宋志四、華陽國志四、水經溫水注合。
At Tanfeng the name should carry the “sword-hilt” graph, but copies substitute the homophone for “hand-bell.” The Song printing and the pronunciation glosses keep the correct graph, and we follow them. That reading matches the upper Han treatise, fascicle five of the Continued Han, fascicle four of the Song gazetteer, book four of the Huayang guo zhi, and the Wen River commentary.
277
永嘉二年至夜郎二郡王遜傳：「元帝加遜安南將軍，刺史如故。 遜表請改分牂牁爲平夷郡，分建寧爲夜郎郡，改益州爲晉寧郡，事皆施行。 」與此志不同。
On the Yongjia-era expansion down to the two Yelang commanderies, Wang Xun’s biography quotes the emperor’s rescript: “The court invested Xun as Defender-in-Chief of the South while leaving him inspector, as before.” He then memorialized to carve Zangge into Pingyi commandery, spin Jianning off as Yelang commandery, and rename Yizhou as Jinning commandery, and every item of the plan was carried out. Yet that narrative disagrees with the arrangement recorded in this chapter.
